exposure: presence or absence of stress urinary incontinence (SUI)
PERFECT scheme variables (power, endurance, repetitions, fast contractions)
transperineal ultrasound variables (bladder neck mobility, H height, ureteric angle, levator anterior area)
outcome: correlation between PERFECT scheme variables, vaginal manometry variables, and transperineal ultrasound variables
differences in these assessment variables between women with and without SUI
cohort: Nonpregnant women aged 18 to 60 years, with and without stress urinary incontinence, excluding those with sphincter deficiency, Oxford scale = 0, and prolapse grade >= 2.
finding: The study found no correlation between ultrasound variables and vaginal manometry or the PERFECT scheme, but significant correlations were observed between specific PERFECT scheme measurements and vaginal manometry, and also among some ultrasound variables.
cross-section timing: At the time of evaluation for each non-pregnant participant.
